extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent prosecution practitioners referencing examiner practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational guidance and standards for preparation of citations, office actions, responses to applicant arguments, and procedural handling during patent examination. Covers citation formats (foreign, nonpatent, electronic), form paragraphs for common argument responses, completeness/clarity of examiner actions, and rules for claim treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official cross-references marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Official cross-references should be marked “X”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use “X” to mark official cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of foreign patents and published applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing foreign patents, the patent number, citation date, name of the country, name of the patentee, and U.S. class and subclass, if appropriate, must be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patents searched in Examining Groups filing by IPC will be cited using the appropriate IPC subclass/group/subgroup. On the file wrapper “Searched” box and PTO-892, the IPC subclass shall be cited in the space provided for “Class”, and IPC group/subgroup shall be cited in the space provided for “Subclass”. If country wrong or omitted, General Reference Branch may assist; date and number often suffice to determine correct country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation when relying on part of a disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When references are furnished and less than the entire disclosure is relied upon, the sheet and page numbers specifically relied upon and the total number of sheets of drawing and pages of specification must be included (except applicant submitted citations). If the entire disclosure is relied on, the total number of sheets and pages are not included, and the appropriate columns on the PTO-892 are left blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify exact pages/sheets relied upon when citing partial disclosures to make clear which portions form basis of the citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of nonpatent publications (books, articles, periodicals)
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing a publication, sufficient information should be given to determine the identity and facilitate the location of the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For books, provide data required by 37 CFR 1.104(d) with specific pages identified together with the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) call number. For periodicals include author(s) and title of the article, title of the periodical, volume number, issue number, date, and pages. If copy relied on is located only in the group, add “Copy in Group — —”. Provide as much bibliographic information as possible so readers can identify and retrieve the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles should not be abbreviated
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use unexplained abbreviations (a citation such as 'P.S.E.B.M.' is meaningless).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal citation allowed only when full details unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Give as much bibliographic information as possible. Minimal information may be used only if the complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal for books: author, title and date. Minimal for periodicals: title of periodical, volume number, date, and pages. Use these only as a last resort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpatent literature with document identification number
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonpatent literature reference with a document identification number is cited, the identification number and the class and subclass should be included on form PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the identification number and class/subclass on PTO-892; provide citation format example such as: (S00840001) Winslow, C.E.A. Fresh Air and Ventilation N.Y., E.P. Dutton, 1926, p. 97-112, TH 7653, W5, 315/22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain office copy of external originals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original publication is located outside the Office, the examiner should immediately make or order a photocopy of at least the portion relied upon and indicate the class and subclass in which it will be filed, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain copy in Office, and indicate class/subclass for filing to ensure the relied-upon material is available in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for electronic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow WIPO Standard ST.14; the format for an electronic document citation is similar to paper but with additional items where appropriate: (A) medium in [ ], (B) retrieval date [retrieved on YYYY-MM-DD], (C) 'Retrieved from' and address, (D) specific passages indicated if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include medium type ([online], [CD-ROM], etc.) after the title or host designation; include retrieval date with four-digit year; include 'Retrieved from' source and address; indicate specific passages when pagination or internal referencing exists. Office copies must be retained if the document may not remain available online. If an electronic document is also available in paper form, it need not be identified as electronic unless desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of electronic citations and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples provided for documents from online databases, Internet, CD-ROMs, bulletin boards, email, product manuals, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examples in MPEP (e.g., WPI [online] with accession numbers; Medline [online] with accession numbers; Internet URLs; CD-ROM citations) as templates for formatting electronic citations and recording retrieval data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of decisions, orders, memoranda and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing court decisions, the USPQ citation should be given and, when convenient, the U.S., CCPA or Federal Reporter citation should also be provided. Manuscript decisions not available to public should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For unpublished but publicly available tribunal decisions, give the tribunal and complete identification of the paper. Decisions found only in patent files should be cited only when there is no published decision on the same point. When citing Commissioner’s orders/notices not yet in the manual, give title, date, and other locating data (e.g., where published).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner’s action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder of invention, fundamental defects, etc.) the action may be limited to such matters before further action is made. Matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the full range of substantive matters when appropriate; for limited circumstances, explain why action is limited. Ensure completeness except for clearly justified limited-scope situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear language when rejecting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim is refused for any reason relating to the merits thereof it should be 'rejected' and the ground of rejection fully and clearly stated, and the word 'rejected' must be used. The examiner should designate the statutory basis for any ground of rejection by express reference to a section of 35 U.S.C. in the opening sentence of each ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected as too broad, give the reason; if indefinite, point out wherein the indefiniteness resides; if incomplete, specify missing elements. Avoid personal comments and expressions of opinion about lack of merit. Do not assert doubts about allowability in the record. Avoid omnibus phrasing and improper grouping of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid improperly expressed rejections (omnibus and grouping)
rubrics_metrics.description: An omnibus rejection of the claim 'on the references and for the reasons of record' is stereotyped and usually not informative and should therefore be avoided. A plurality of claims should never be grouped together in a common rejection, unless that rejection is equally applicable to all claims in the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specific grounds and reasons; avoid boilerplate and grouping that obscures which claims are rejected for which reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note all outstanding requirements in each action
rubrics_metrics.description: In taking up an amended application for action the examiner should note in every letter all the requirements outstanding against the application. Every point in the prior action of an examiner which is still applicable must be repeated or referred to, to prevent the implied waiver of the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat or reference prior outstanding points; require correction of informalities as soon as allowable subject matter is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer material traversed by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the requirements are traversed, or suspension thereof requested, the examiner should make proper reference thereto in his or her action on the amendment. Where the applicant traverses any rejection, the examiner should, if he or she repeats the rejection, take note of the applicant's argument and answer the substance of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the substance of applicant’s arguments; if applying prior rejection to new/amended claims, specifically identify the ground (by citing paragraph in former Office letter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Answering asserted advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant's reply includes arguments and affidavits that prior art does not teach or inherently yield one or more advantages urged for patentability, the examiner should state reasons why the asserted advantages are without significance in determining patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state reasons in the record so applicant and, if appealed, the Board, know the examiner considered and weighed the asserted advantages. Failure to rebut may result in the advantage being accepted on appeal (case law examples cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid piecemeal examination where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecemeal examination should be avoided as much as possible. The examiner ordinarily should reject each claim on all valid grounds available, avoiding, however, undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply major technical rejections (lack of disclosure, undue breadth, indefiniteness, res judicata) when appropriate, fully developing reasons rather than offering mere conclusions. Exceptions permitting limited action include: application too informal, undue multiplicity of claims (no successful election), misjoinder (no successful election), and perpetual motion disclosures. When certain rejections like res judicata or new matter apply, accompany with rejections on all other available grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of inaccuracies in amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When inaccuracies exist in an amendment, notify the applicant (see MPEP § 714.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures in MPEP § 714.23 to point out inaccuracies and requirements for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each claim must be mentioned in every letter
rubrics_metrics.description: In every letter, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given. Each action should conclude with a summary of all claims presented for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep claim history traceable; update Index of Claims as set forth in MPEP § 719.04. Treat claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 or 1.146 per cited MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: State when claims are allowable and suggest corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should identify any claims which he or she judges, as presently recited, to be allowable and/or should suggest any way in which he or she considers that rejected claims may be amended to make them allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pro se applications, examiners may draft one or more claims and indicate they would be allowed if incorporated. If claim is allowable except for form, offer definite suggestions for correction and consider interviews to accelerate agreement on allowable claims. Do not delay allowance of clearly allowable claims once prior art fully developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling incorrect citation of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an error in citation of a reference is brought to the attention of the Office by applicant, a letter correcting the error, together with a correct copy of the reference, is sent to applicant. Where the error is discovered by the examiner, applicant is also notified and the period for reply restarted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner corrects the error, in ink, in the paper in which the error appears, places initials on the margin, and notes the paper number of the action in which the citation has been correctly given. Use form paragraphs 7.81-7.83 as appropriate; if erroneous citation not formally corrected, correct by examiner’s amendment accompanying Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for declassified printed matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Declassified material usually has two dates: the printing date (preparation for limited distribution) and the publication date (date of release to the public). The date of release following declassification is the effective date of publication for statutory purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(a), declassified material may be prima facie evidence of prior knowledge as of its printing date even though classified at that time; such printing date is not an absolute statutory bar and may be antedated by affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131. If date of release not shown, determine via Office of Technical Services or other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for unpersuasive arguments (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.37 through 7.38 may be used where applicant's arguments are not persuasive or are moot. These paragraphs require the examiner to state that applicant's arguments have been considered but are not persuasive (or are moot due to new grounds of rejection) and to provide explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using form paragraphs, precede with required paragraph numbers and fill in bracketed placeholders (e.g., restate applicant's argument, provide explanation). Ensure the examiner addresses all arguments not previously responded to in the statement of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Age of Reference(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contentions that the reference patents are old are not impressive absent a showing that the art tried and failed to solve the same problem notwithstanding its presumed knowledge of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicant argues references are old, require a showing that the art tried and failed to solve the same problem. Use form paragraph 7.37.01 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Bodily Incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for obviousness is not whether the features of a secondary reference may be bodily incorporated into the structure of the primary reference; rather the test is what the combined teachings of the references would have suggested to those of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond by explaining the combined teachings rationale and cite In re Keller and related case law. Use form paragraph 7.37.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Hindsight Reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Any judgment on obviousness is in a sense necessarily a reconstruction based upon hindsight reasoning. But so long as it takes into account only knowledge which was within the level of ordinary skill at the time the claimed invention was made, and does not include knowledge gleaned only from the applicant’s disclosure, such a reconstruction is proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that hindsight is inappropriate only when examiner relies on applicant’s disclosure beyond what was known at the time; use form paragraph 7.37.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: No Suggestion To Combine
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness can only be established by combining or modifying the teachings of the prior art where there is some teaching, suggestion, or motivation to do so found either in the references themselves or in the knowledge generally available to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicant argues no suggestion to combine, identify where motivation or suggestion is found (in references or general knowledge). Use form paragraph 7.37.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Nonanalogous Art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art reference must either be in the field of applicant’s endeavor or, if not, then be reasonably pertinent to the particular problem with which the applicant was concerned, in order to be relied upon as a basis for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant alleges a reference is nonanalogous, explain why it is analogous or reasonably pertinent to the problem. Use form paragraph 7.37.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Number of References
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on a large number of references in a rejection does not, without more, weigh against the obviousness of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that sheer quantity of references is not dispositive; the combination and teaching are what matter. Use form paragraph 7.37.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Applicant Obtains Result Not Contemplated by Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that applicant has recognized another advantage which would flow naturally from following the suggestion of the prior art cannot be the basis for patentability when the differences would otherwise be obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant argues a novel advantage, explain whether that advantage renders claims nonobvious or instead flows naturally from prior art. Use form paragraph 7.37.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Limitations Which Are Not Claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: The features upon which applicant relies that are not recited in the rejected claim(s) cannot be read into the claims; limitations from the specification are not read into the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicant relies on unclaimed features, restate those features and explain they are not part of the claim. Use form paragraph 7.37.08.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Intended Use
rubrics_metrics.description: A recitation of the intended use of the claimed invention must result in a structural difference between the claimed invention and the prior art in order to patentably distinguish the claimed invention from the prior art. In a claim drawn to a process of making, the intended use must result in a manipulative difference as compared to the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that intended-use arguments show structural or manipulative differences; use form paragraph 7.37.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Limitation(s) in Preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: A preamble is generally not accorded any patentable weight where it merely recites the purpose of a process or the intended use of a structure, and where the body of the claim does not depend on the preamble for completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant relies on preamble language, explain why preamble does or does not impart patentable weight. Use form paragraph 7.37.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: General Allegation of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(b) when they amount to a general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifically pointing out how the language of the claims patentably distinguishes them from the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require specific point-by-point explanation of patentable distinctions rather than general allegations. Use form paragraph 7.37.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Novelty Not Clearly Pointed Out
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(c) when they do not clearly point out the patentable novelty the claims present in view of the prior art or how amendments avoid such references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clarity regarding claimed novelty relative to cited art. Use form paragraph 7.37.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Against References Individually
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot show nonobviousness by attacking references individually where the rejections are based on combinations of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that arguments must address the combination as applied; use form paragraph 7.37.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and attachments for informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms (PTO-948 and PTO-152) listing informalities noted by the Draftsperson and the Office of Initial Patent Examination are attachments to the examiner's first action and should be mailed with that action. Any additional formal requirements the examiner desires should be included in the first action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these forms with the examiner’s first action and ensure any formal requirements are communicated at that time.
